medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Gastroparesis admission hydration and glucose monitoring
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Gastroparesis admission hydration and glucose monitoring
Requested action: 0.9% sodium chloride IV at 100 mL/hour initially for dehydration; reassess within 4 hours using vital signs, examination and urine output. Strict intake/output. POC glucose every 4 hours while intake poor; notify for BG <70 or >300, rising anion gap, worsening vomiting or altered mental status. Vital signs every 4 hours. If oral intake remains poor or glucose falls, contact physician to adjust dextrose-containing fluids while maintaining basal insulin.

Order for: Admission electrolyte replacement
Requested action: Potassium chloride 20 mEq IV once, diluted as 10 mEq in 100 mL normal saline for each of two consecutive bags, each over 1 hour (total 20 mEq over 2 hours); use infusion pump, never IV push. Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV once over 2 hours for magnesium 1.7 mg/dL. Confirm urine output and renal function before replacement. Recheck potassium/magnesium after replacement before additional doses; target K >4 and Mg >2 per H&P.
Metoprolol tartrate 50 mg PO every 12 hours for atrial fibrillation rate control. Hold for HR <60 bpm, SBP <100 mmHg or symptomatic hypotension and notify physician.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Therapeutic unfractionated heparin infusion for LV thrombus
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Therapeutic unfractionated heparin infusion for LV thrombus
Requested action: Continue unfractionated heparin IV infusion at 18 units/kg/hour using verified dosing weight, then titrate by institutional therapeutic heparin nomogram to anti-Xa 0.3–0.7 IU/mL. Pharmacy must verify weight, bag concentration, pump rate and current infusion before administration. No additional bolus for this continuation order. Check anti-Xa 6 hours after initiation or any rate change, then per protocol once stable; monitor CBC/platelets and bleeding. Hold infusion and notify physician for active bleeding, acute neurologic change or excessive anticoagulation per protocol.

medicalOrders.order_name: Cardiology - New atrial fibrillation, EF35% and LV thrombus
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: New atrial fibrillation, EF35% and LV thrombus
Requested action: Evaluate rate/rhythm strategy, LV thrombus anticoagulation and long-term transition plan, new systolic dysfunction and possible ischemic cause. Review prior GI bleed/fall risk and initiate appropriate HF guideline-directed therapy as hemodynamics allow.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - AF and anticoagulation admission monitoring
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: AF and anticoagulation admission monitoring
Requested action: Continuous telemetry; vital signs every 4 hours. Daily weights and strict intake/output. Fall precautions, walker and assisted ambulation. Monitor for bleeding, melena, hematuria, neurologic change, hypotension or symptomatic bradycardia; notify physician promptly. Therapeutic heparin monitoring per infusion order.

medicalOrders.order_name: Physical Therapy - Deconditioning and gait safety
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Deconditioning and gait safety

medicalOrders.order_name: Occupational Therapy - ADLs and discharge safety
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: ADLs and discharge safety
Requested action: Assess ADLs, equipment needs and home safety given deconditioning and fall history.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Psychiatric admission safety and wound care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Psychiatric admission safety and wound care
Requested action: Suicide/self-harm precautions; at least every-15-minute safety checks with observation level reassessed by psychiatry and continuous observation if risk warrants. Remove sharps and unsafe objects, provide calm supportive environment and therapeutic engagement. Vital signs each shift; assess superficial forearm wounds and provide local cleansing/dressing as needed. Monitor and report signs of alcohol withdrawal or medical change.

medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Psychiatric admission and aftercare support
Requested action: Assess psychosocial stressors, housing/supports and barriers to care. Coordinate outpatient psychiatry, DBT-based therapy and substance-use treatment resources. Obtain collateral only with appropriate consent; assist with individualized safety and discharge plan.
Extended-release valproate admission regimen: intended final order is 1,000 mg PO nightly; configuring exact extended-release schedule in order editor.

medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Buspirone and hypertension medication reconciliation
Requested action: Verify buspirone dose, route and dosing frequency with prior records; current order lists 7.5 mg once daily without route. Reconcile antihypertensive medications and allergies. Continue verified escitalopram10mgPOdaily; communicate confirmed regimen to psychiatrist.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Baseline COPD oxygen and psychiatric safety
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Baseline COPD oxygen and psychiatric safety
Requested action: Oxygen via nasal cannula continuously at 2 L/min per home/admission regimen. Keep upright with head of bed elevated and wedge pillow. Vital signs and SpO2 at least every 4 hours and as needed; assist with oxygen adherence using calm explanation and redirection. Notify physician for SpO2 below 90%, increasing work of breathing, cyanosis or altered mental status; obtain medical evaluation if persistent despite prescribed oxygen. Standard psychiatric safety checks. Monitor sedation and respiratory status with PRN lorazepam/risperidone; hold sedating PRNs and call physician for respiratory depression or excessive sedation.

medicalOrders.order_name: Respiratory Therapy - COPD oxygen and inhaler assessment
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: COPD oxygen and inhaler assessment
Requested action: Review baseline2Lnasalcannula oxygen requirement, inhaler technique and tiotropium formulation/dose; current medication entry lists1puff without strength or device. Confirm appropriate device-specific regimen with prescriber. Assist with oxygen adherence and reassess respiratory status if symptoms change.

medicalOrders.order_name: Social Work - Psychosis and chronic oxygen discharge planning
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Psychosis and chronic oxygen discharge planning
Requested action: Assess supports and ability to manage psychiatric medications, inhaler and home oxygen safely. Coordinate outpatient follow-up and appropriate assistance once stabilized, with patient participation and collateral consent as applicable.

Order for: Risperidone admission regimen
Requested action: Risperidone 3 mg PO nightly at bedtime, scheduled. Separate PRN dose: risperidone 1 mg PO every 4 hours as needed for agitation, reassessing after each dose. Notify prescriber after 3 PRN doses in 24 hours. Review recent antipsychotic and benzodiazepine administration before additional PRNs; hold for excessive sedation and contact prescriber. Catalog has no selectable frequency for risperidone.

Lorazepam 1 mg PO every 4 hours as needed for agitation. Notify prescriber after 3 PRN doses in 24 hours. Review cumulative sedative exposure before dosing; hold for excessive sedation or RR <12/min. Use verbal de-escalation first and reassess after each dose.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Psychiatric admission safety and sedation monitoring
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Psychiatric admission safety and sedation monitoring
Requested action: Standard psychiatric safety observations, calm structured environment, verbal de-escalation and hygiene assistance. Assess level of consciousness, respirations, vital signs and recent medication administration before sedating PRNs and reassess afterward. Notify prescriber after 3 PRN doses in 24 hours, or immediately for oversedation, hypoxia, fever, rigidity or acute mental-status change. Do not automatically repeat prior ED IM medications.

medicalOrders.order_name: Social Work - Psychiatric stabilization and aftercare
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Psychiatric stabilization and aftercare
Requested action: Clarify housing, supports and outpatient treatment; coordinate psychiatric follow-up and offer cannabis-use counseling after stabilization. Obtain collateral with appropriate consent.
Clonidine 0.1 mg PO every 6 hours AS NEEDED for opioid-withdrawal symptoms. Hold for SBP <100 mmHg, HR <60 bpm, dizziness or symptomatic hypotension; reassess BP and symptoms after dose.

For withdrawal-associated diarrhea: give 4 mg PO after the first loose stool, then 2 mg PO after each subsequent loose stool as needed. Maximum 16 mg in 24 hours. Stop when diarrhea resolves; hold and reassess for fever, bloody stool, ileus or abdominal distension.
Ondansetron 4 mg PO every 8 hours as needed for withdrawal-related nausea. Reassess persistent symptoms and consider QT risk with other medications/electrolyte abnormalities.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Admission opioid withdrawal and suicide-safety monitoring
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Admission opioid withdrawal and suicide-safety monitoring
Requested action: Standard psychiatric safety checks with suicide-risk reassessment. COWS and vital signs every 4 hours and as needed, and reassess symptoms and BP about 1 hour after clonidine. Encourage oral fluids and light food as tolerated. Notify clinician for worsening withdrawal, inability to hydrate, hypotension, confusion or respiratory depression. Use supportive de-escalation; medication treatment for opioid use disorder requires clinician assessment and a separate order.

medicalOrders.order_name: Social Work - Opioid-use treatment and aftercare
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Opioid-use treatment and aftercare
Requested action: Assess housing, insurance and supports; arrange discussion of medication treatment for opioid use disorder, recovery support and outpatient follow-up. Plan overdose education and take-home naloxone at discharge.
Propranolol 10 mg PO three times daily, admission home regimen. Hold for HR <60, SBP <100, symptomatic hypotension or excessive lethargy and notify clinician.
Aripiprazole 15 mg PO daily, established admission regimen. Monitor mental status, sedation and adverse effects.
Clonazepam 1 mg PO every 12 hours, established admission regimen. Assess alertness and respiration before dosing; hold for excessive sedation or RR <12/min and notify clinician.

Order for: Psychiatric admission medication monitoring
Requested action: Standard psychiatric safety observations. Vital signs and alertness assessment each shift and before sedating medications. Monitor respiratory rate and sedation with clonazepam/valproate and BP/heart rate with propranolol. Notify physician promptly for new reduced responsiveness, hypoxia, hypotension, bradycardia, fever or rigidity; do not give additional sedatives in that setting.

Order for: Divalproex ER 1000 mg nightly
Requested action: Divalproex sodium EXTENDED-RELEASE 1,000 mg PO once nightly at bedtime, established admission regimen. Swallow extended-release tablets whole. Do not substitute immediate-release divided dosing. Assess sedation; hold and notify clinician for acute reduced responsiveness or respiratory depression. Written order used because the medication catalog only offers divided schedules and edits to newly placed catalog orders do not persist.

Apply one nicotine 21 mg/24-hour transdermal patch daily for baseline tobacco dependence. Remove old patch before applying new patch and rotate sites. Document refusal and notify clinician for significant intolerance.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Nicotine gum 2 mg PRN cravings
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Nicotine gum 2 mg PRN cravings
Requested action: Nicotine gum 2 mg buccally every 2 hours as needed for breakthrough nicotine cravings, in addition to the prescribed patch. Chew slowly and park between cheek and gum; do not swallow the gum. Maximum 12 pieces in 24 hours under this order. Reassess nausea, palpitations or other intolerance.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Olanzapine 5 mg PO PRN agitation
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Olanzapine 5 mg PO PRN agitation
Requested action: Olanzapine 5 mg PO every 6 hours AS NEEDED for agitation after verbal de-escalation and reassessment. Continue existing scheduled 10 mg nightly. Maximum total olanzapine 20 mg in 24 hours from all scheduled and PRN doses unless psychiatrist gives a separate order. Hold for excessive sedation and notify clinician.

Lithium carbonate EXTENDED-RELEASE 900 mg PO once nightly at bedtime, per admission regimen. Maintain hydration; monitor renal function, sodium and lithium level as clinically indicated. Verify formulation and dosing history.

Order for: Mania admission monitoring
Requested action: Routine psychiatric safety checks, monitor sleep and behavior, and encourage therapeutic milieu participation. Vital signs each shift. Encourage adequate oral hydration while taking lithium and document intake concerns, medication refusal, nicotine cravings, adverse effects or escalating agitation. Assess alertness before sedating PRNs.

Haloperidol 5 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for severe agitation after de-escalation. Review total scheduled and PRN doses; notify psychiatrist before total exceeds 20 mg/24h. Reassess sedation, extrapyramidal symptoms and QT risk. IM alternative requires assessment when oral medication cannot be given; do not give duplicate PO and IM doses.

Order for: Haloperidol scheduled admission dose
Requested action: Haloperidol 5 mg PO twice daily (every 12 hours), scheduled treatment for first-episode psychosis. Separate PRN haloperidol order is not a substitute for scheduled dosing. Review cumulative exposure, monitor EPS and sedation, and notify psychiatrist before total haloperidol exceeds 20 mg/day. Catalog lacks a scheduled twice-daily option.

Lorazepam 1 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for anxiety. Hold for excessive sedation or respiratory rate <12/min and notify clinician. Assess medical causes of new symptoms before giving additional sedatives.

Order for: First-episode psychosis admission monitoring
Requested action: Standard psychiatric safety checks and routine vital signs. Monitor treatment response, sedation and abnormal movements; notify clinician for new neck/jaw stiffness, oculogyric movements, swallowing/breathing difficulty, fever, rigidity or acute mental-status change. Use de-escalation and assess before additional PRN medication.

Location: 12-lead ECG. Indication: admission baseline before antipsychotic treatment for first-episode psychosis. Source-defined QTc430ms; otherwise normal sinus rhythm without acute ischemic changes. Do not incorporate later dystonia event or repeat-study findings.
Hydroxyzine 25 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for anxiety. Hold for excessive sedation, dizziness or symptomatic hypotension; review additive sedation with trazodone.
AS NEEDED ONLY: trazodone 50 mg PO once nightly at bedtime for insomnia. Hold for excessive sedation, dizziness or symptomatic hypotension.

Order for: Prazosin 1 mg PO nightly
Requested action: Prazosin 1 mg PO once nightly at bedtime for trauma-related nightmares, admission starting dose. Check BP; hold for SBP <100 mmHg, symptomatic dizziness or hypotension and notify clinician. Assist with ambulation and counsel to rise slowly.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - PTSD/depression admission safety and hydration
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: PTSD/depression admission safety and hydration
Requested action: Standard psychiatric safety checks and suicide-risk reassessment. Encourage oral food and fluids, monitor intake and hydration, and assist with ambulation as needed. Counsel to rise slowly from lying/sitting, especially after bedtime medications. Record routine vital signs and notify clinician for dizziness, presyncope, falls or poor intake.
Thiamine 100 mg IV daily for 3-5 days, then transition to 100 mg PO daily when eating reliably. Give promptly; do not delay urgent glucose treatment to administer thiamine.

Alcohol withdrawal: 1 mg PO every 4 hours PRN CIWA-Ar 8-15. Reassess CIWA, sedation, respiratory rate and oxygenation 1 hour after dose. Hold for excessive sedation, RR <12, or hypoxemia and notify provider. Notify provider promptly for CIWA >15, hallucinations, seizures or worsening symptoms to reassess and escalate treatment.
Nausea/vomiting.

Order for: Multivitamin supplementation
Requested action: Multivitamin with minerals: 1 tablet PO daily.

Order for: Alcohol withdrawal admission care
Requested action: CIWA-Ar and vital signs every 4 hours, and reassess 1 hour after lorazepam. Seizure, aspiration and fall precautions; suicide safety checks every 15 minutes. Encourage oral hydration and regular diet as tolerated; notify provider if unable to maintain intake. Notify immediately for CIWA >15, hallucinations, seizure, confusion, respiratory depression or unstable vital signs.

Order for: Electrolyte replacement
Requested action: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 2 hours once for admission hypomagnesemia. Potassium chloride 40 mEq PO once for K 3.3, if tolerating oral intake. Confirm renal function and adequate urine output; reassess electrolytes after replacement.
Constipation prevention during clozapine therapy. Hold for diarrhea.
Constipation prevention. Hold for diarrhea.
PRN pain or fever only; maximum 3 g/day from all sources. Notify provider for any new fever during clozapine treatment.

Order for: Clozapine baseline monitoring
Requested action: Routine psychiatric safety checks; monitor daily bowel movements, orthostatic symptoms and adverse effects. Weekly CBC with differential/ANC during early clozapine treatment per current prescribing information. Escalate new fever, sore throat, chest pain, dyspnea or persistent tachycardia promptly.
Wheezing or shortness of breath; no active asthma exacerbation.

Order for: Admission liver injury monitoring
Requested action: Regular age-appropriate diet and oral hydration as tolerated. Vital signs and neurologic checks every 4 hours; strict intake/output. Avoid acetaminophen and NSAIDs pending liver injury evaluation. Notify provider for altered mentation, bleeding, hypoglycemia or clinical deterioration. Obtain detailed OTC medication dosing history.

Order for: Pediatric hepatology evaluation
Requested action: Admission marked transaminitis with INR 1.8 without encephalopathy; evaluate cause and synthetic dysfunction, monitoring and transfer criteria.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Initial liver injury diagnostic workup
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Initial liver injury diagnostic workup
Requested action: Obtain admission acetaminophen level, hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen and core IgM, hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, EBV testing and urinalysis. These results are not supplied by the source case and should remain pending rather than be assumed negative. Trend CMP, PT/INR and glucose daily. Further autoimmune/metabolic testing guided by pediatric hepatology; ammonia if altered mentation.

Location: right upper quadrant/liver with Doppler. Indication: admission marked transaminitis and INR 1.8; assess liver architecture, biliary dilation and hepatic/portal vascular patency. Baseline simulation: no biliary ductal dilation, patent hepatic and portal vessels, no focal hepatic mass; do not infer a specific cause of hepatitis or later encephalopathy.

Order for: Pediatric acetaminophen PRN
Requested action: Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg/dose PO every 6 hours PRN fever or discomfort, maximum 60 mg/kg/day. Use verified current measured weight; record absolute mg and formulation volume before administering.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Pediatric hydration and viral illness care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Pediatric hydration and viral illness care
Requested action: Dextrose 5% in 0.9% sodium chloride IV at weight-based maintenance: 4 mL/kg/hour for first 10 kg, 2 mL/kg/hour for next 10 kg, 1 mL/kg/hour above 20 kg. Obtain current weight and verify pump rate before starting. Adjust to oral intake and urine output; strict intake/output and wet diaper counts. Regular age-appropriate diet, oral rehydration. Contact/droplet precautions for rhinovirus; vital signs every 4 hours. No repeat bolus without reassessment.
Nausea/vomiting. Source admission regimen; reassess ongoing need and avoid simultaneous PRN antiemetic stacking.
Second-line nausea/vomiting if ondansetron ineffective; do not administer simultaneously with other sedating PRNs. Verify weight, review QT-risk medications and monitor for dystonia or sedation.

Order for: Home hydroxyzine bedtime regimen
Requested action: Hydroxyzine 25 mg PO at bedtime, per documented prior home regimen. Monitor for sedation; review additive QT-risk medications.

Order for: Vomiting admission hydration
Requested action: Normal saline 0.9% IV continuous at 80 mL/hour per existing admission regimen, reassess against measured weight and oral intake. Strict intake/output, daily weights, vital signs every4hours. Advance to gluten-free diet as tolerated. Monitor electrolytes daily during ongoing emesis.

Order for: Home amitriptyline reconciliation
Requested action: Confirm home amitriptyline dose and schedule for migraine prophylaxis before continuing; dose absent from source H&P and existing orders. Review all medications for additive QT prolongation and sedation; verify pediatric dosing weight.

Order for: Pediatric gastroenteritis PRN medications
Requested action: Acetaminophen15mg/kg/dose PO every6hours PRN pain/fever, max60mg/kg/day. Ondansetron0.15mg/kg/dose PO every8hours PRN vomiting preventing oral rehydration, max4mg/dose. Verify measured dosing weight and formulation volumes.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Gastroenteritis hydration and intake monitoring
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Gastroenteritis hydration and intake monitoring
Requested action: D5 normal saline IV at maintenance by measured weight (4mL/kg/h first10kg,2mL/kg/h next10kg,1mL/kg/h above20kg); verify actual pump rate. Use isotonic maintenance rather than D5 half-normal saline given Na134. Adjust to oral intake, strict intake/output, daily weights, regular age-appropriate diet as tolerated. Routine peripheral IV site checks; contact precautions while diarrhea persists.
Nasal congestion; gently suction before feeds and sleep as needed. Avoid deep suction.

Order for: Infant acetaminophen PRN
Requested action: Acetaminophen15mg/kg/dose PO every6hours PRN fever/discomfort; max60mg/kg/day. Verify current measured weight and formulation volume.

Order for: Bronchiolitis supportive care
Requested action: Bronchiolitis pathway. Pulse oximetry while asleep; assess work of breathing with vitals every4hours and PRN. Gentle nasal suction/repositioning as needed. Breast milk/formula PO ad lib in small frequent feeds; strict intake/output. Reassess hydration if intake inadequate. Low-flow nasal cannula oxygen starting0.5-1L/min only for persistent SpO2 below90% after suction/repositioning, titrate to at least90%; notify provider for increasing support, apnea or distress. Contact/droplet precautions.
At bedtime. Continue established home basal regimen; do not omit basal insulin in type1 diabetes. Coordinate adjustments with pediatric endocrine when NPO.
Left foot cellulitis. Verify dosing weight and renal function.
PRN pain or fever only; verify weight-based maximum 60mg/kg/day or3g/day, whichever is lower.

Order for: Infant acetaminophen PRN
Requested action: Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg/dose PO every 6 hours PRN fever/discomfort, maximum 60 mg/kg/day. Verify measured dosing weight and formulation volume before administration.
3,200 mg piperacillin plus 400 mg tazobactam IV every 6 hours; 100 mg piperacillin/kg/dose at 32 kg. Monitor renal function.

Order for: Post-PICU appendicitis floor care
Requested action: Regular age-appropriate diet as tolerated. D5 normal saline IV at weight-based maintenance (4 mL/kg/h first10kg,2mL/kg/h next10kg,1mL/kg/h above20kg), adjusted to oral intake; document measured weight and verify pump rate. Strict intake/output, vital signs every4hours, postoperative wound and PICC care. Follow surgical activity instructions. Notify provider for respiratory change, hypotension or poor perfusion.

Order for: Type1 diabetes peri-procedure monitoring
Requested action: Carbohydrate-consistent diet until NPO after midnight for planned sedated foot MRI. Point-of-care glucose before meals and bedtime; every4hours while NPO. D5NS IV75mL/hour while NPO per previous regimen, adjust with endocrine to glucose and hydration. Hold nutritional rapid-acting insulin while NPO; continue basal insulin. Notify provider promptly for glucose<70 or>250, symptoms or ketosis; use pediatric hypoglycemia protocol when indicated.

Order for: Planned left foot MRI
Requested action: MRI left foot for cellulitis with concern for deeper infection/osteomyelitis; planned next morning with sedation as in source case. Remain pending until performed; no admission MRI result should be generated. Coordinate fasting and insulin/dextrose plan.
Scheduled postoperative pain control. Confirm dosing weight; max60mg/kg/day, not more than3g/day.

Order for: Pediatric postoperative antiemetic
Requested action: Ondansetron0.15mg/kg/dose PO or IV every8hours PRN nausea/vomiting, maximum4mg/dose. Use one route per dose; verify measured weight and formulation.
3.375g IV every8hours by extended infusion over4hours for postoperative perforated ulcer; verify renal function and surgical duration.

Order for: Admission potassium replacement
Requested action: Potassium chloride10mEq in100mL IV over1hour, repeat for4doses (total40mEq) for K3.0 while NPO. Verify adequate urine output and renal function; recheck potassium and magnesium after replacement, adjust further dosing to results.

Order for: Cardiac home medication reconciliation
Requested action: Verify home CAD/HTN/CHF medications, allergies and last doses. Coordinate resumption with surgery given recent ulcer perforation/bleeding and NPO status.

Order for: Pediatric insulin regimen verification
Requested action: Verify home insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio, correction factor, glucose target and current weight; these are absent from source and cannot be inferred from prior lispro dose1unit. Coordinate rapid-acting meal/correction orders with pediatric endocrinology before dosing. Home glargine18units nightly documented in prior orders.
15 mg/kg/dose for 28 kg. Infuse over 15 minutes for fever/pain when unable to tolerate oral medication. Maximum 1680 mg/day from all routes.

Order for: Pediatric antiemetic PRN
Requested action: Ondansetron0.15mg/kg/dose IV every8hours PRN nausea/vomiting, maximum4mg/dose. Verify measured weight and review QT risk.

Order for: Post-tonsillectomy overnight care
Requested action: Continuous pulse oximetry overnight for OSA. Vital signs every4hours and monitor for bleeding, airway compromise and oral intake. Clear liquids, advance as tolerated per ENT. D5NS with20mEq/L KCl IV60mL/hour per previous regimen after verifying weight, renal function and urine output; reduce with adequate oral intake. Avoid NSAIDs per case surgical plan. Notify ENT promptly for any bleeding or airway symptoms.

Order for: Colostomy reversal perioperative care
Requested action: NPO as directed by surgery; allow essential transplant medications with sips per operative plan. Glucose checks every6hours while NPO, vital signs every4hours, strict intake/output, serial abdominal exams, SCDs and assisted ambulation. DailyCBC/BMP; coordinate tacrolimus trough drawn before morning dose when requested. Hold metformin while NPO.

Order for: Febrile neutropenia admission care
Requested action: Vital signs every4hours with close reassessment for instability; strict intake/output and daily weights. D5NS IV at weight-based maintenance after verifying measured weight and pump rate; adjust to oral intake and clinical status. Neutropenic/contact precautions, central port care, gentle oral saline rinses for mucositis. Daily CBC with differential; follow admission blood cultures already obtained. Notify oncology promptly for lethargy, perfusion changes, hypotension or new source.

Order for: Postoperative PRN medications
Requested action: Morphine2mg IV every2hours PRN severe pain (score>7); reassess pain, sedation, respiration and oxygenation. Hold for oversedation, RR<12 or hypotension. Ondansetron4mg IV every6hours PRN nausea.

Order for: Perforated ulcer postoperative care
Requested action: NPO; NG tube to low intermittent suction. Normal saline IV100mL/hour, reassess for CHF/volume overload. Strict intake/output, daily weights, JP drain to bulb suction and record output. Vital signs every4hours. Bilateral SCDs, assisted mobility/fall precautions, incentive spirometry while awake. Telemetry during electrolyte replacement.

Sensitive correction: glucose<=150 no insulin;151-200:1unit;201-250:2units;251-300:3units;301-350:4units;351-400:5units;>400:6units and notify provider. No nutritional insulin while NPO. Do not stack rapid-acting doses within4hours; use hypoglycemia protocol for glucose<70.
Continue established10unit basal regimen; reassess dose for fasting and glucose trend with treating team.
Acute cholecystitis; extended infusion over4hours. Verify renal function/CrCl and adjust if indicated. Replaces discontinued ciprofloxacin per workbook admission plan.

Sensitive correction: glucose<=150 none;151-200:1unit;201-250:2units;251-300:3units;301-350:4units;351-400:5units;>400:6units and notify. No nutritional dose while NPO. Reassess for glucose<70; no dose stacking within4hours.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Admission nausea and potassium replacement
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Admission nausea and potassium replacement
Requested action: Ondansetron4mg IV every4hours PRN nausea per admission plan; reassess QTc/electrolytes and avoid other QT-prolonging agents. Potassium chloride10mEq in100mL IV over1hour, repeat for2doses(total20mEq) initially for K3.1 with AKI. Confirm urine output; recheck potassium after replacement before additional doses.

Order for: Cholecystitis admission monitoring
Requested action: NPO except medications allowed by surgery; strict intake/output, vital signs every4hours, glucose every6hours while NPO. Coordinate laparoscopic cholecystectomy with surgery. Reassess pain and sedation after opioids; oxycodone5mg for mild-moderate OR10mg for severe pain, never both for same episode; IV hydromorphone only breakthrough.

Order for: Postoperative breakthrough pain regimen
Requested action: Oxycodone5mg PO every4hours PRN moderate/severe pain. Hydromorphone0.2mg IV every3hours PRN severe breakthrough pain only if oral regimen inadequate. Reassess sedation, RR and pain after dose; hold for excessive sedation or RR<12. Continue scheduled acetaminophen, maximum3g/day.
Postoperative nausea/vomiting.
Reduce/discontinue as oral intake becomes adequate; monitor volume status.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Low anterior resection postoperative care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Low anterior resection postoperative care
Requested action: Clear liquid diet, advance as tolerated per colorectal pathway. Routine wound care, vital signs every4hours and strict intake/output. Maintain Foley overnight, remove POD1 morning per surgical plan and monitor first void. SCDs, early assisted ambulation, out of bed to chair and incentive spirometry while awake. MorningCBC/BMP per service.
VTE prophylaxis. Verify weight, renal function, platelet trend and surgical bleeding risk; hold for active bleeding or procedure as directed.

Order for: Trauma postoperative maintenance care
Requested action: Dextrose5% in0.45% sodium chloride IV100mL/hour per source postoperative regimen; reassess sodium, volume status and oral intake daily. Monitor surgical wounds, leg neurovascular status, intake/output and vital signs every4hours. SCDs if permitted by orthopedic injuries. Coordinate postsplenectomy vaccination planning before discharge.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Morphine IV PCA postoperative analgesia
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Morphine IV PCA postoperative analgesia
Requested action: Morphine IV PCA: patient demand dose1mg, lockout10minutes, no basal infusion, maximum6mg/hour from patient demands. No automatic loading or clinician bolus. Confirm prior opioid exposure, renal function and ability to understand/use PCA before continuation; use clinician-directed alternative if confused. Monitor sedation, respiration and pulse oximetry; hold for oversedation or RR<12 and notify provider.
Postoperative pain/fever; maximum3g/day. Obtain temperature and reassess any new fever before masking a possible transfusion reaction.

Order for: Postoperative anemia baseline care
Requested action: Lactated Ringers IV100mL/hour, reassess volume status/intake. Strict intake/output and vital signs every4hours; postoperative wound care, SCDs and assisted mobility. Use separate IV access for LR during transfusion; normal saline only in blood administration line.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Packed red blood cell transfusion for postoperative anemia
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Packed red blood cell transfusion for postoperative anemia
Requested action: Transfuse1unit crossmatch-compatible leukoreduced PRBC IV over2-3hours for Hgb6.5g/dL. Verify consent, current type/screen, product compatibility and bedside identity checks before starting. Baseline vital signs, observe closely for first15minutes and monitor per transfusion protocol. Normal saline only in blood line. Reassess hemoglobin/clinical response after unit; no automatic second unit.

Order for: Trauma medication reconciliation
Requested action: Verify perioperative cefazolin indication/duration; active order lacks dose and frequency, and source does not specify an ongoing course. Confirm PCA regimen, anticoagulant dosing and home medications.
VTE prophylaxis after confirming postoperative hemostasis. Hold and notify surgery for active bleeding or unexplained ongoing hemoglobin fall; adjust for renal impairment.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Morphine IV PCA baseline analgesia
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Morphine IV PCA baseline analgesia
Requested action: Morphine IV PCA demand1mg,10minute lockout, no basal infusion, maximum6mg/hour. No loading dose or automatic clinician bolus. Verify prior regimen and patient ability to self-dose; monitor sedation, respirations and pulse oximetry. Hold for excessive sedation or RR<12 and reassess.
Nausea/vomiting; reassess abdomen if new or worsening symptoms.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Small bowel resection postoperative care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Small bowel resection postoperative care
Requested action: NPO; continueLR100mL/hour and adjust to intake/output and volume status. Strict intake/output, vital signs every4hours, serial abdominal exams and bowel-function assessment. Routine incision care, SCDs and assisted mobilization per surgery.
Severe breakthrough pain. Reassess pain/sedation/respirations; hold for oversedation, RR<12 or hypotension.

Premeal glucose<=150:0units;151-200:1;201-250:2;251-300:3;301-350:4;351-400:5;>400:6andnotify. Bedtime<=200:0;201-250:1;251-300:2;>300:3,notifyif>400. WhileNPO useq6h premeal scale, no nutritional doses. Do not stack within4hours; hypoglycemia protocol if<70.
VTE prophylaxis after confirming surgical hemostasis and adequate renal function.

Order for: Whipple postoperative baseline care
Requested action: Normal saline IV100mL/hour while intake inadequate; reassess daily and reduce with diet advancement. Advance diet per surgical plan, strict intake/output, daily weights, wound/drain care, assisted mobility and SCDs. Vital signs every4hours. Glucose before meals and bedtime, every6hours ifNPO.
Established home regimen. Hold for SBP<100, acute kidney injury or hyperkalemia; review renal function and potassium.
Moderate/severe postoperative pain despite acetaminophen. Use minimum effective dose in older adult; hold for excessive sedation or respiratory depression.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Femur ORIF postoperative baseline care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Femur ORIF postoperative baseline care
Requested action: Vital signs every4hours, routine neurovascular and wound checks, assisted mobility/fall precautions, SCDs and intake/output monitoring. Maintain orientation aids and sleep/wake routine. PT/OT and weight-bearing status per orthopedic team.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - ED psychiatric hold and safety
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: ED psychiatric hold and safety
Requested action: Maintain documented psychiatric hold and continuous observation/sitter, suicide precautions and secure belongings per ED protocol. Consistent-carbohydrate diet. Monitor vital signs every4hours and report any new medical symptoms.

Order for: Psychiatric hold evaluation
Requested action: Suicidal ideation with specific ingestion plan and schizoaffective disorder; assess risk and arrange inpatient psychiatric placement.

Order for: Psychiatric placement
Requested action: Coordinate inpatient psychiatric bed and safe transfer during ED hold.

Severe psychosis/agitation after de-escalation fails, per source ED hold plan. Monitor QTc, electrolytes and sedation; reassess before repeat dosing and notify provider if persistent agitation. IV use requires monitored setting.

Order for: Toxic encephalopathy admission monitoring
Requested action: Continuous telemetry and pulse oximetry after sedation; frequent mental-status/respiratory assessments and vital signs. Strict intake/output. Monitor hydration, CK and renal/electrolyte trends; use low-stimulation environment and fall precautions.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Admission hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia replacement
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Admission hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia replacement
Requested action: Potassium chloride10mEq in100mL IV over1hour for4doses(total40mEq) for admissionK2.8. Magnesium sulfate2gIV over2hours once for admissionMg0.8mEq/L. Verify renal function and urine output; recheck electrolytes after replacement before further dosing. Continuous telemetry.

Location: head/brain without IV contrast. Indication: initial altered mental status and severe agitation. Admission baseline finding documented in ED note: no acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect or other acute intracranial abnormality.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - RLQ abdominal pain ED baseline care
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: RLQ abdominal pain ED baseline care
Requested action: NPO. Lactated Ringers IV125mL/hour. Vital signs and serial abdominal examinations per ED protocol; monitor intake/output and pain. Prior fentanyl50microgramsIV was a completed single dose; no automatic redose.

Order for: Acute decompensated HFrEF
Requested action: EF25% with pulmonary edema/hypoxemia, BNP1640 and K2.8; review diuresis and GDMT, medication reconciliation and electrolyte management.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Pending CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Pending CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
Requested action: Location: abdomen and pelvis. Indication: right lower quadrant pain, anorexia andWBC16 with concern for appendicitis. CT with IV contrast is pending at sign-out; no admission report is available. Preserve pending status and do not insert contrast-reaction findings into baseline.

Order for: Pending trauma CT studies
Requested action: CT head without contrast: evaluate intracranial hemorrhage after MVC on apixaban. CT cervical spine without contrast: evaluate fracture after MVC with neck pain. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast: evaluate occult blunt trauma. These studies are pending at admission/sign-out; do not fabricate a negative cervical-spine result or mark the collar cleared.

Order for: Heart failure admission monitoring
Requested action: Oxygen2L/min nasal cannula, titrate to SpO2 92-96%. Continuous telemetry/pulseox, strict intake/output, daily weights, low-sodium consistent-carbohydrate diet, glucosebeforemeals/bedtime. Monitor renal function/electrolytes during diuresis.

medicalOrders.order_name: Nursing - Trauma observation and cervical precautions
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Trauma observation and cervical precautions
Requested action: Lactated Ringers IV75mL/hour. Maintain cervical collar and spine precautions until imaging reviewed and clinician documents clearance. Serial neurologic examinations and vital signs per ED trauma observation protocol. Hold apixaban pending trauma evaluation. Avoid NSAIDs; prior acetaminophen650mgPO was already given.

medicalOrders.order_name: General - Sensitive lispro correction with meals
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Sensitive lispro correction with meals
Requested action: Insulin lispro SC before meals: glucose<=150 no insulin;151-200:1unit;201-250:2;251-300:3;301-350:4;351-400:5;>400:6andnotify. Check bedtime glucose and notify for correction plan if elevated. No nutritional dose whileNPO; do not stack rapid-acting doses within4hours.
Established admission antihypertensive/HFrEF regimen; monitor blood pressure, renal function and potassium. Hold for SBP<100 or acute renal deterioration.

ACS infusion; initial maximum1000units/hour, then titrate per ACS nomogram to aPTT60-80seconds or institution-calibrated target. Verify measured dosing weight and current pump rate. Initial60unit/kg bolus(max4000units) was part of ED initiation; do not repeat automatically. aPTT6hours after initiation/rate changes, dailyCBC/platelets and bleeding checks.
Persistent severe chest pain after clinician reassessment; monitor BP, respiratory rate and sedation. Notify provider immediately for recurrent ischemic symptoms.
Maintenance after325mg loading dose already given in ED.

Order for: ACS admission monitoring
Requested action: Continuous telemetry; vital signs per chest-pain protocol, monitor for bleeding on heparin. NPO after midnight for possible coronary study; glucosebeforemeals/bedtime andq6hwhenNPO. Serial troponin/ECG per ACS pathway; urgent clinician reassessment for recurrent pain or instability.

Order for: Suspected NSTE-ACS
Requested action: Exertional chest pressure, diabetes and new ST depressions with initial negative troponin. Review antithrombotics and coronary angiography versus CCTA plan; no later STEMI findings at admission.

Location:12-lead ECG. Indication: initial exertional chest pressure. Admission baseline: sinus rhythm82bpm with new ST depressions compared with prior ECG; no ST elevation. Do not include later STEMI changes.
Location: chest. Indication: initial chest pain evaluation. Admission baseline: no acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

Order for: Post-allergic-reaction ED observation
Requested action: Continue planned6-hour observation after initial EMS/ED treatment. Monitor vital signs, airway, breathing, circulation and skin symptoms; continuous pulse oximetry while observed. Notify clinician immediately for recurrent swelling, wheeze, vomiting, hypotension or respiratory symptoms. Confirm measured weight.

Order for: Allergy discharge planning
Requested action: Before discharge, provide peanut-allergy avoidance counseling and epinephrine auto-injector teaching/prescription with weight-appropriate device. Verify current weight:0.15mg device for15-30kg,0.3mg for>=30kg; select lower-weight device per labeling if<15kg. Arrange allergy follow-up. Do not discharge before observation complete and clinician reassessment.

Order for: Possible ectopic pregnancy
Requested action: Initial stable presentation with abdominal pain/spotting,beta-hCG1635,Hgb9.5,Rhnegative,and noIUP with questionableleftadnexalmass. Review urgently and advise management; recommendations pending at sign-out.

Order for: Early pregnancy bleeding observation
Requested action: NPO pending OB assessment; maintain IV access and close vital-sign monitoring. Record bleeding, pain and intake/output. Initial1LIVfluid and morphine4mg were already administered per source; no automatic repeat. Notify provider immediately for worsening pain, syncope, hypotension or tachycardia.

Location: pelvis, transvaginal ultrasound. Indication: initial early pregnancy with left-sided abdominal pain and vaginal spotting,beta-hCG1635. Source baseline: no intrauterine gestational sac and questionableleftadnexalmass, concerning for ectopic pregnancy/pregnancy of unknown location. Do not insert later rupture or hemorrhagic-shock findings.

Order for: Rho(D) immune globulin
Requested action: Rho(D) immune globulin300micrograms(1500IU) IM once within72hours forRh-negative pregnancy with bleeding/suspected ectopic, after confirming Rh type, antibody screen and no prior sensitization. Verify product and OB plan; this is maternal prophylaxis.
Severe fracture pain; reassess pain, neurovascular status, sedation and respiration. Hold for oversedation, RR<12 or hypotension.

Order for: Tibial fracture admission care
Requested action: Normal saline IV150mL/hour; reassess hydration and urine output. Maintain splint/immobilization, non-weight-bearing right leg and assisted mobility. Neurovascular checks every2hours; notify orthopedics for change from intact baseline. NPO after midnight for planned fixation.

medicalOrders.order_name: Orthopedic Surgery - Closed right tibial shaft fracture
medicalOrders.instructions:
Order for: Closed right tibial shaft fracture
Requested action: Displaced midshaft right tibial fracture after motorcyclecollision; initially2+DP/PTpulses and intact sensation/strength. Plan operative repair next day and pain control; follow splint and activity instructions.

Location: right tibia/fibula. Indication: motorcyclecollision with lower-leg pain. Initial source finding: closed displaced midshaft right tibial fracture. Do not add later compartment-syndrome findings.

imagingStudies.report:
Exam: Chest X-ray, single frontal view.
Indication: Patient status post urology procedure for infected kidney stone, now clinically deteriorating with tachycardia and fever.
Technique: Portable anteroposterior chest radiograph obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: The lungs are clear without focal consolidation or effusion. No pneumothorax or pleural abnormality identified. Cardiac silhouette is within normal limits. No acute bony abnormalities. Ureteral stent string is visible externally as noted clinically.
Impression: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality to explain current clinical deterioration. Continued close monitoring and further evaluation for sepsis or other complications related to recent urologic intervention recommended.

Exam: X-ray clavicle
Indication: Patient status post urology procedure for infected kidney stone, now with concern for fractured clavicle.
Technique: Standard anteroposterior and oblique views of the clavicle obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: There is a non-displaced fracture of the midshaft of the right clavicle. No significant displacement or comminution noted. Surrounding soft tissues appear unremarkable. No evidence of pneumothorax or other acute thoracic injury.
Impression: Non-displaced midshaft fracture of the right clavicle. No acute complications identified on this exam.

Exam: Electrocardiogram (EKG)
Indication: Tachycardia with heart rate of 112 bpm in a pediatric patient; evaluation for arrhythmia or ischemic changes.
Technique: Standard 12-lead EKG obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Sinus tachycardia at a rate of approximately 112 beats per minute. Normal axis. No evidence of acute ischemic changes, ST segment elevations, or depressions. No pathological Q waves. PR and QT intervals within normal limits for age. No arrhythmias or conduction blocks identified.
Impression: Sinus tachycardia without acute ischemic or arrhythmic abnormalities. Clinical correlation recommended; cardiology consultation is appropriate given tachycardia and clinical context.

imagingStudies.order_name: Thoracic spine x-ray:  Compression fracture at T3 without obvious malalignment or gross instability.

imagingStudies.report:
Exam: Thoracic spine X-ray.
Indication: Evaluation for suspected compression fracture.
Technique: Standard anteroposterior and lateral views of the thoracic spine.
Comparison: None.
Findings: There is a compression fracture involving the T3 vertebral body characterized by loss of anterior vertebral height without evidence of malalignment or gross instability. The remaining thoracic vertebrae demonstrate normal alignment and bone density. No acute paraspinal soft tissue swelling is noted.
Impression: Compression fracture of the T3 vertebral body without malalignment or gross instability.

Exam: Bilateral Hip X-ray
Indication: Right hip pain and suspected fracture in a patient with known osteoporosis.
Technique: Anteroposterior views of both hips obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: There is a displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the right proximal femur. The left hip shows degenerative changes with decreased bone density consistent with osteoporosis. No acute fracture is identified on the left side. Joint spaces are preserved bilaterally. Soft tissues are unremarkable.
Impression: Displaced intertrochanteric fracture of the right hip in the setting of underlying osteoporosis. No acute abnormality on the left hip.

Exam: EKG
Indication: Chest pain, non-ischemic, normal
Technique: Standard 12-lead electrocardiogram obtained and analyzed.
Comparison: None
Findings: Sinus rhythm with a heart rate of 88 bpm. No acute ischemic changes, no arrhythmias, and no conduction abnormalities identified. QT interval within normal limits.
Impression: Normal EKG with sinus rhythm and no evidence of acute ischemia or arrhythmia.

Exam: Chest X-ray, portable.
Indication: Hematemesis in a patient with suspected alcoholic pancreatitis and recent tachycardia.
Technique: Anteroposterior view obtained at bedside.
Comparison: None.
Findings: There is mild bilateral pulmonary vascular congestion with interstitial edema. No focal consolidation or pleural effusion identified. Cardiac silhouette is within normal limits. No pneumothorax or acute bony abnormalities.
Impression: Mild pulmonary edema/congestion likely related to volume status and possible early heart strain in the setting of acute illness. No acute cardiopulmonary process requiring immediate intervention identified.

Exam: Right upper quadrant (RUQ) ultrasound.
Indication: Fever, leukocytosis, and clinical suspicion of acute cholecystitis.
Technique: Ultrasound examination of the right upper quadrant was performed using a high-frequency transducer.
Comparison: None.
Findings: The gallbladder is distended with a thickened wall measuring up to 5 mm. There is pericholecystic fluid present. Sonographic Murphy's sign is positive. Multiple gallstones are noted within the gallbladder lumen without evidence of biliary ductal dilation. The common bile duct measures within normal limits. No hepatic lesions or intrahepatic biliary dilation identified.
Impression: Findings are consistent with acute cholecystitis. Clinical correlation and surgical consultation are recommended.

Exam: Chest X-ray, frontal and lateral views.
Indication: Fever, leukocytosis, elevated neutrophils, and tachycardia.
Technique: Standard posteroanterior and lateral chest radiographs obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: The lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. The cardiac silhouette is normal in size and contour. The mediastinum and hila are unremarkable. No acute bony abnormalities identified.
Impression: Normal chest radiograph. No radiographic evidence of pneumonia or acute cardiopulmonary process. Clinical correlation recommended given elevated white blood cell count and fever.

Exam: Electrocardiogram (EKG)
Indication: Sinus tachycardia with mild QT prolongation; fever and elevated white blood cell count suggest possible infection.
Technique: Standard 12-lead EKG performed.
Comparison: None.
Findings: The EKG demonstrates sinus tachycardia with a heart rate of approximately 105 bpm. There is mild prolongation of the QT interval. No acute ischemic changes or arrhythmias noted. The rhythm is otherwise regular.
Impression: Sinus tachycardia with mild QT prolongation, likely related to underlying febrile illness and systemic inflammatory response. Recommend clinical correlation and monitoring of QT interval, especially if medications that prolong QT are initiated.

Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast.
Indication: Evaluation of abdominal pain and postoperative status.
Technique: Contrast-enhanced CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis was performed.
Comparison: None.
Findings: There is a rectal mass identified, consistent with colorectal cancer. No evidence of bowel obstruction or perforation. No significant lymphadenopathy or distant metastatic disease is noted. Postoperative changes are present consistent with recent cholecystectomy. Bowel gas pattern is normal with positive bowel sounds on clinical exam.
Impression: Rectal mass consistent with colorectal cancer. No acute postoperative complications identified on imaging.

Exam: Portable AP chest radiograph
Indication: Chest pain; acute coronary syndrome
Technique: Single portable AP view of the chest.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for technique. Lungs are clear without focal air-space opacity, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. No acute osseous abnormality identified.
Impression: No acute cardiopulmonary process.

Exam: Right hand X-ray.
Indication: Evaluation for fracture or foreign body following trauma.
Technique: Standard two-view radiographs of the right hand obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: No evidence of acute fracture or dislocation identified. No radiopaque foreign body visualized. Soft tissues demonstrate mild swelling without gas or other abnormality.
Impression: No fracture or foreign body detected. Mild soft tissue swelling noted, consistent with soft tissue injury.

Exam: PA and lateral chest radiographs.
Indication: Fever, cough, dyspnea, and asthma exacerbation; concern for community-acquired pneumonia.
Technique: Frontal and lateral radiographs of the chest obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Focal right lower lobe airspace opacity concerning for consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: Right lower lobe pneumonia. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

Exam: 12-lead ECG
Indication: Hyperglycemia, hyponatremia, and suspected volume overload/heart failure.
Technique: Standard 12-lead ECG obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Sinus rhythm at approximately 85 bpm. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ST-segment elevation or depression. No significant T-wave abnormalities. QRS and QT intervals are within normal limits.
Impression: Sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. No acute ischemic ECG changes.

Exam: PA and lateral chest radiographs
Indication: Cough, fever, dyspnea; COVID-19 infection. Initial admission evaluation.
Technique: Two-view chest radiographs obtained.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits. Lungs are clear without focal air-space consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. No acute osseous abnormality identified.
Impression: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

Exam: CT Abdomen and Pelvis without contrast.
Indication: Persistent nausea and vomiting in a patient with known gastroparesis and type 1 diabetes mellitus.
Technique: Axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained without intravenous contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: No evidence of bowel obstruction or dilatation. No focal inflammatory changes or free fluid. No masses or acute intra-abdominal pathology identified. The stomach is not markedly distended. No evidence of pneumoperitoneum. Normal appearance of the liver, spleen, pancreas, kidneys, and adrenal glands.
Impression: No acute abdominal abnormality identified to explain symptoms. Findings are consistent with prior imaging and support a diagnosis of gastroparesis flare in the clinical context. No evidence of obstruction or other surgical abdomen.

Exam: 12-lead Electrocardiogram (EKG)
Indication: Evaluation of cardiac rhythm and QT interval in a patient with type 1 diabetes mellitus and gastroparesis flare presenting with nausea and vomiting.
Technique: Standard 12-lead EKG performed.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Sinus tachycardia with a heart rate of approximately 110 bpm. QTc interval measured at 432 ms, within normal limits. No evidence of ischemic changes, arrhythmias, or conduction abnormalities.
Impression: Sinus tachycardia with normal QTc interval in the clinical context of nausea and vomiting likely related to gastroparesis flare. No acute cardiac abnormalities identified.

Exam: Transthoracic echocardiogram (ultrasound of the heart)
Indication: Known reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%) and suspected left ventricular thrombus
Technique: Standard transthoracic echocardiographic views were obtained including parasternal long axis, short axis, apical four-chamber, and subcostal views. No contrast agent was used.
Comparison: None
Findings: Left ventricular systolic function is severely reduced with an estimated ejection fraction of approximately 35%. There is a well-defined, echogenic mass adherent to the left ventricular apex consistent with thrombus. No pericardial effusion is identified. Right ventricular size and function appear within normal limits. Valvular structures show no significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Impression: Severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an estimated EF of 35%. Presence of left ventricular apical thrombus confirmed. Findings correlate with clinical history and ongoing anticoagulation therapy. Recommend continuation of current management and clinical correlation.

Exam: Portable AP chest radiograph
Indication: Dizziness, palpitations, intermittent mild dyspnea
Technique: Single frontal chest radiograph obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits for technique. Lungs are clear without focal air-space opacity, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. No pulmonary edema. No acute osseous abnormality identified.
Impression: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

Exam: Chest radiographs, PA and lateral views.
Indication: Orthopnea; suspected congestive heart failure; elevated BNP.
Technique: Two-view chest radiography without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Mild enlargement of the cardiac silhouette. Mild pulmonary vascular/interstitial prominence. No focal air-space consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.
Impression: Mild cardiomegaly with pulmonary vascular/interstitial congestion. No focal pneumonia or large pleural effusion.

Exam: 12-lead electrocardiogram
Indication: Admission baseline prior to antipsychotic therapy.
Technique: Standard 12-lead ECG obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal cardiac axis and intervals. QTc measures approximately 430 ms. No acute ST-segment or T-wave abnormalities.
Impression: Normal sinus rhythm without acute ischemic changes. QTc approximately 430 ms.

Exam: 12-lead electrocardiogram
Indication: Initial exertional chest pressure.
Technique: Standard 12-lead ECG obtained at rest.
Comparison: Prior ECG from 3 months earlier.
Findings: Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm. New ST-segment depressions involving the anterolateral leads compared with the prior tracing. No ST-segment elevation. No significant arrhythmia or high-grade AV block.
Impression: Abnormal ECG demonstrating sinus rhythm with new ischemic ST-segment depressions. No STEMI pattern identified on this tracing.

Exam: Right tibia and fibula radiographs, 2 views
Indication: Motorcycle collision with right lower-leg pain.
Technique: AP and lateral radiographs of the right tibia and fibula.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Acute displaced fracture of the mid diaphysis of the right tibia with approximately one shaft-width displacement and mild angulation. No definite additional fracture identified. Soft-tissue swelling of the lower leg.
Impression: Acute displaced midshaft fracture of the right tibia with surrounding soft-tissue swelling.

Exam: 12-lead electrocardiogram
Indication: Dizziness and palpitations.
Technique: Standard 12-lead ECG obtained without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Normal sinus rhythm at approximately 80 beats per minute. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-segment or T-wave abnormalities. No evidence of acute ischemia.
Impression: Normal sinus rhythm. No acute ischemic changes.

Exam: CT head without intravenous contrast.
Indication: Altered mental status and severe agitation.
Technique: Noncontrast axial CT images of the head obtained with multiplanar reformations.
Comparison: None.
Findings: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline shift. Gray-white matter differentiation is preserved. Ventricles and sulci are within normal limits for age. Basal cisterns are patent. No acute calvarial abnormality. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.
Impression: No acute intracranial abnormality.

Exam: CT abdomen and pelvis without intravenous contrast
Indication: Abdominal distension, pain, nausea and vomiting; prior laparotomies; suspected adhesive small-bowel obstruction. Acute kidney injury.
Technique: Noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis with multiplanar reformatted images.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Multiple dilated fluid-filled small-bowel loops measuring up to approximately 4.0 cm with a transition point in the mid abdomen, compatible with mechanical small-bowel obstruction, likely adhesive in etiology. No pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free intraperitoneal air, or definite closed-loop configuration. Mild adjacent mesenteric edema. Decompressed distal small bowel and colon. Postsurgical changes of splenectomy, cholecystectomy, and ventral abdominal wall repair. No hydronephrosis. Evaluation for bowel-wall enhancement and ischemia is limited without intravenous contrast.
Impression: 1. Mechanical small-bowel obstruction with a mid-abdominal transition point, favored adhesive. 2. No free air or definite CT evidence of closed-loop obstruction. 3. Noncontrast technique limits assessment for bowel ischemia.

Exam: Right upper quadrant abdominal ultrasound
Indication: Right upper quadrant pain, positive Murphy sign, fever, and leukocytosis.
Technique: Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound evaluation of the right upper quadrant was performed.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Multiple gallstones are present. The gallbladder wall is thickened with a small amount of pericholecystic fluid. Positive sonographic Murphy sign. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation identified.
Impression: Sonographic findings consistent with acute calculous cholecystitis. No biliary ductal dilatation.

Exam: Right upper quadrant abdominal ultrasound with hepatic Doppler
Indication: Marked transaminitis and coagulopathy (INR 1.8); assess liver architecture, biliary dilation, and hepatic/portal vascular patency.
Technique: Grayscale and color/spectral Doppler sonographic evaluation of the right upper quadrant and hepatic vasculature.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Liver is normal in size with homogeneous echotexture and smooth contour. No focal hepatic lesion identified. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Common bile duct measures 2 mm. Gallbladder is unremarkable without cholelithiasis, wall thickening, or pericholecystic fluid. No right upper quadrant free fluid. Hepatic veins are patent with appropriate flow. Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. Hepatic artery is patent with appropriate flow. Visualized IVC is unremarkable.
Impression: 1. Unremarkable sonographic appearance of the liver and biliary tree. 2. Patent hepatic and portal veins with appropriate Doppler flow. 3. No focal hepatic lesion or biliary ductal dilatation.

Exam: Renal and bladder ultrasound
Indication: Initial febrile urinary tract infection; evaluate for hydronephrosis or structural abnormality.
Technique: Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the bilateral kidneys and urinary bladder.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Right kidney measures 5.7 cm and left kidney measures 5.8 cm in length, appropriate for age. Normal renal parenchymal echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation bilaterally. No focal renal lesion, calculus, or hydronephrosis. Urinary bladder is adequately distended and appears unremarkable without wall thickening or focal abnormality. No free fluid identified.
Impression: Normal renal and bladder ultrasound. No hydronephrosis or structural abnormality identified.

Exam: Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound
Indication: Early pregnancy with left-sided abdominal pain and vaginal spotting; beta-hCG 1,635.
Technique: Transvaginal grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the pelvis was performed.
Comparison: None.
Findings: The uterus is anteverted and normal in size. No intrauterine gestational sac, yolk sac, or fetal pole is identified. Endometrium measures approximately 11 mm. A questionable heterogeneous left adnexal structure measures approximately 2.1 cm, without definite discrete gestational sac or fetal cardiac activity. The right ovary is unremarkable. No significant free pelvic fluid is identified.
Impression: No intrauterine pregnancy visualized. Questionable left adnexal mass, concerning for ectopic pregnancy in the setting of positive beta-hCG and left-sided pain. Findings represent a pregnancy of unknown location. Recommend correlation with serial beta-hCG and short-interval follow-up ultrasound as clinically indicated.

Exam: Chest radiographs, PA and lateral views.
Indication: COPD; baseline evaluation in patient on home oxygen.
Technique: Two-view chest radiography without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits. Lungs are hyperinflated with flattening of the diaphragms, compatible with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. No focal air-space opacity, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. No acute osseous abnormality identified.
Impression: Chronic hyperinflation/COPD changes without acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

imagingStudies.order_name: Portable AP chest — right subclavian CVC position and postplacement complication assessment; result pending
imagingStudies.report:
Exam: Portable AP chest radiograph
Indication: Right subclavian central venous catheter position and postplacement complication assessment.
Technique: Single portable AP view of the chest.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Right subclavian central venous catheter tip projects over the lower SVC. Medium-sized right pneumothorax is present. Trachea remains midline without mediastinal shift. No large pleural effusion. Mild bibasilar postoperative atelectatic changes.
Impression: Medium-sized right pneumothorax without radiographic evidence of tension. Right subclavian central venous catheter tip projects over the lower SVC.
